text:
nate: quick heads-up — after landing the token-phase budget change (80% decode cap) on canary, decode tail latency jumped ~8% on long-seq jobs.
maria: hmm, which canary? tag/commit?
nate: canary-2026-03-19 / sha 8f3a2b4. repro on rtx-4g, seq=12k workloads. saw more kernel stalls in the flamegraph.
maria: can you paste the flame snippet or hotspot names?
nate: pasted a tiny slice:
```
gpu_kernel_prefill  12%
gpu_kernel_decode   54%  -> stalls waiting on KV lookup path
kv_cache_lock       18%  -> high contended wait
cuda_memcpy_async   8%
others              8%
```
maria: KV lock at 18% is new. Did the token-budget change alter batch formation so decode batches pack more heterogeneous seqs?
liam: possibility: token-budget tweak caused larger decode groups to be formed because prefill quotas shrank, so gen-phase gets more mixed-length batches -> more KV thrash and kernel context switches.
sasha: early thought: we previously coupled prefill and decode thresholds. If prefill now yields smaller batches, decode absorbing requests may increase head-of-line variance. Suggest separating the queue admission thresholds and giving decode a stricter max-batch-size and a shorter queue-wait window.
maria: agree. also consider bumping KV priming window: currently kv_warm_ms=50, maybe increase to 150ms for decode-heavy workloads to reduce cold hits.
liam: tradeoff: longer warm window can hurt latency for very short sessions. maybe make it phase-aware: prefill warm window=30ms, decode warm window=150ms.
nate: ran a quick microbench: decode max-batch-size 64 -> tail down by 5% but throughput drops 4%. decode max-batch-size 32 -> tail down 11%, throughput -9%.
sasha: can we try adaptive: target decode batch size based on observed seq variance in the queue? e.g., if stddev(lengths) > X then cap batch size lower.
maria: sounds good. we should also check kernel selector: some of those decode batches got routed to the fallback kernel path (quantized fallthrough) more often. maybe affinity mapping got skewed by larger batches.
perf-bot: [alert] canary-2026-03-19: end-to-end p99 latency increased 9% vs baseline on staging cluster-3.
liam: next steps I propose:
- nate: collect two flamegraphs (baseline vs canary) + full perf trace (nvprof) for one long run
- sasha: prototype phase-aware queue params + adaptive batch cap (PR draft)
- maria: patch kernel-affinity rule to prefer stable kernel for decode-heavy batches (small change)
- liam: run 12-hour canary with workload mix A/B and compare p50/p95/p99
nate: I already uploaded nvprof traces to /tmp/canary-traces/8f3a2b4 and a short summary in ops-drive: link: https://drive.redwood.ai/trace/8f3a2b4
sasha: I'll open a draft PR tonight: draft branch token-phase-adapt. will add a feature flag so we can roll back quickly.
maria: ping @liam when PR is up; I'll review kernel-affinity change and run local microbench.
liam: if adaptive cap looks promising, we can gate it behind per-queue heuristics and target a 5% tail reduction without >5% throughput loss.
sasha: if we need quick rollback, revert the token-budget change and re-run canary. but I'd rather iterate with feature flags.
nate: one more datapoint — KV eviction rate spiked slightly during regression window. I think larger decode batches are causing more transient cache churn.
maria: ok let's try phase-aware warm windows + adaptive decode cap first. If that reduces KV evictions and kernel fallthroughs, we keep it behind flag.
liam: created ticket INF-2026: token-phase-queue-choreography with tasks assigned. I'll schedule a canary tonight at 23:00 PST.
sasha: thanks. i'll post PR link once created. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: [note] scheduled canary run at 2026-03-19T23:00:00Z on staging cluster-3. monitor: perf-alerts channel.
nate: thanks team — will follow up with trace details and an A/B summary after the run.
